To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optimal jacket temperature profile is of the bang–bang type, that the optimal switching positions are located in the middle of the reactor, and that the optimal control law is not very sensitive to dispersion.

(i) the optimal control law for the jacket fluid temperature of a dispersive tubular reactor is bang-bang, (ii) the optimal bang-bang switching positions depend on the dispersion and on the reactor temperature profile.

(1) optimal control of a tubular reactor with a bang-bang temperature profile can be obtained using the Pontryagin minimum principle; (2) the bang-bang switching point is optimised by a weighted shooting-type algorithm, ensuring the Danewkerts boundary conditions are fulfilled; and (3) the optimal temperature control profiles obtained for the tubular reactor with different degrees of axial dispersion, are compared.

the development of a generalised methodology for the optimal design of tubular chemical reactors with dispersion, based on Pontryagin’s minimum principle, which can be extended to other reactor types.
the determination of the optimal steady-state and transient temperature profiles for the jacket fluid of a tubular chemical reactor.
the determination of the optimal control laws for the tubular reactor, which are practically feasible, in order to achieve a better understanding of the impact of dispersion.
